name: Baobab QR
author: baobabqr

sections.description:
Baobab QR puts a QR code on any page of your site. Add the Baobab QR code block, or the shortcode [baobab_qr], and the page shows a QR code that opens it, with its short address under it if you like.

Each code is a website link code in your own Baobab QR account, on your plan, so you can see its scans, change its design and, on a paid plan, where it goes. Baobab QR checks every link before a code goes live, and its codes keep working even if you stop paying.

  • One code per page, made the first time the page is shown, and kept.
  • A code for any other link: [baobab_qr url="https://example.com/menu/"], or the block’s Link setting.
  • Visitors only ever see a working code. If a code can’t be made, they see nothing, and your site’s editors see why and what to do.
  • No tracking, no cookies and no scripts on your pages: the code is a picture.

You need a Baobab QR account, free or paid. A free account keeps 3 codes, and each page with a code uses one. See the plans at https://baobabqr.com/pricing/.

External services

This plugin relies on Baobab QR (https://baobabqr.com), run by Ruan Francois (Pty) Ltd, to make each page’s QR code in your Baobab QR account. It contacts Baobab QR only after you save a site key in Settings, Baobab QR.

What is sent, and when: the address of the page (or the link you gave the code), with your site key, to https://baobabqr.com/api/site/codes, the first time a code is needed for that address. The plugin then asks again once a day while the page is being shown (every 10 minutes while a code isn’t live yet), so a new design or a finished check reaches your page; Baobab QR answers with the same code. WordPress also sends your site’s address in its user agent, as it does with every request it makes. Nothing about your visitors is sent.

Baobab QR’s Terms: https://baobabqr.com/legal/terms/
Baobab QR’s Privacy Policy: https://baobabqr.com/legal/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Sign in to Baobab QR at https://baobabqr.com/app/settings/, and under Your WordPress sites make a site key. Copy it: it’s shown only once.
  3. In WordPress, go to Settings, Baobab QR, paste the key and press Save key.
  4. Add the Baobab QR code block to a page, or type [baobab_qr] where the code should go.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Baobab QR account?

Yes. The codes are made in your account, so they keep working and you can manage them there. A free account keeps 3 codes; paid plans keep more.

What can the shortcode do?

[baobab_qr] shows a code for the page it’s on. url="https://example.com/" gives it another link, address="yes" shows the short address under it, and size="200" sets its width in pixels (80 to 600; 160 if you leave it out).

When is a page’s code made?

The first time the page is shown once it’s published, in the editor’s preview or to a visitor. A draft gets no code, because its address changes when it’s published.

What do visitors see if a code can’t be made?

Nothing. Your site’s editors see a short note in its place saying why, for example that the plan’s codes are used up, and what to do.

What happens if I delete a page’s code in Baobab QR?

The page gets a new code the next time it’s shown. To stop showing a code, take the block or shortcode off the page.

What happens if I remove the site key?

Pages that already have a code keep showing it, and the codes keep working. Pages without one get no new code until you add a key.

Does the plugin track my visitors?

No. It adds no cookies or scripts to your pages, and sends nothing about your visitors anywhere. Baobab QR counts the scans of each code as your code’s tracking setting allows, without storing anyone’s IP address.
